subject.title: [Bug]: Slack `allowBots: true` silently drops all bot messages unless `allowFrom` contains an explicit owner user ID

question: Should Slack support an explicit owner-presence bypass for bot-authored room messages, or should wildcard-only `allowBots` setups remain fail-closed with better diagnostics?
rationale: The current behavior is a documented security guard for Slack bot relays, but it silently breaks real automation workflows; automation should not choose between fail-closed security, warning-only UX, and a new all-bot admission mode without maintainer intent.

options.title: Warn and preserve guard
options.body: Add Slack doctor/startup/config UI diagnostics for wildcard-only or ownerless `allowBots` setups while keeping explicit owner presence or per-channel bot allowlists required for room bot messages.

options.title: Add explicit all-bot mode
options.body: Introduce `allowBots: "all"` as an intentionally unsafe opt-in that skips owner-presence authorization while preserving mention rules and bot loop protection.

options.title: Treat wildcard as owner presence
options.body: Let wildcard `allowFrom` satisfy the room bot gate, restoring intuitive wildcard behavior but weakening the prior owner-presence security boundary for existing configs.

recommendation.title: Warn and preserve guard
recommendation.body: Add Slack doctor/startup/config UI diagnostics for wildcard-only or ownerless `allowBots` setups while keeping explicit owner presence or per-channel bot allowlists required for room bot messages.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the owner-presence guard and are the clearest history-backed owner for the security/compatibility choice.
